summary: Verified the iter62 HIGH fix. GET /live-dispatch/readiness now returns a live_calling_stop_off check. It is ok=false when live_calling_stop is True, 'false' (a string), None, 0 or missing, and ok=true only when the value is exactly False. POST /live-dispatch/authorize still returns 423 under the phase lock, requires auth and CSRF (missing header or a foreign Origin gives 403), and its audit row's preconditions now include live_calling_stop_off with the correct bool. The independence matrix (a)-(d) holds across /safety-status, the /switches blockers and readiness. Switch endpoints reject wrong typed phrases (400), require auth and CSRF, save to ai_call_settings _id=global, and write audit rows. Backend: 50/50 pass across the 4 regression suites plus the new iter63 suite, run serially. Frontend: the Settings rows safety-row-test-permit and safety-row-live-stop show the correct text. On the Live page, the confirm button stays disabled with a wrong phrase. Releasing and re-engaging Live Stop, and enabling and revoking Test Calling, both save across reload. The readiness-live_calling_stop_off item shows on the Live > Automatic Calling Queue tab with a red X while the stop is ON. DB ended in its initial safe state: emergency_stop=True, live_calling_stop=True, test_calling_permitted=False, ai_live_enabled=False, live_dispatch_authorized=False, ai_test_enabled=True (as it was at the start). AI_CALLING_ENABLED=false. No real calls or messages were sent.

minor.issue: The blocker and checklist logic is still duplicated in 4 places. They agree now, but they can drift again. evaluate_live() is still not called from production code.
